test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to ______, the Parliament amended the Constitution (42nd Constitutional Amendment) and inserted 'Secular', 'Socialist', and 'Integrity' in the Preamble of the Constitution.
solution:
The correct answer is "**Article 368**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Parliament was given** unrestrained power** to amend any parts of the Constitution** without judicial review**.
 
• This essentially invalidated the Supreme Court's ruling in **Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala **in 1973. 
 
• The amendment to article 368 prevented any constitutional amendment from being **"called in question in any Court on any ground"**.
 
• It also declared that there would be **no limitation **whatever on the constituent power of Parliament to amend the Constitution.
 
• The 42nd Amendment also restricted the power of the courts to issue stay orders or injunctions.
 
• The 42nd Amendment revoked the courts' power to determine what constituted an office of profit.
 
• A new article 228A was inserted in the Constitution which would give High Courts the authority to** "determine all questions as to the constitutional validity of any State law".**
 
• The amendment's fifty-nine clauses stripped the** Supreme Court **of many of its powers and moved the political system toward parliamentary **sovereignty.**
 
• The 43rd and 44th Amendments reversed these changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 359:**

 
 
• ​During a **National Emergency**, the president is permitted by Article 359 to suspend the ability to petition any court to enforce fundamental rights.
 
• This indicates that only their enforcement is stopped by Article 359 and not the Fundamental Rights themselves.
 
• Although the right to seek redress is suspended, the aforementioned rights technically still exist.
 
• Only those Fundamental Rights mentioned in the Presidential Order are subject to the suspension of enforcement.
 
• The suspension may also be for the duration of the emergency or for a shorter time period specified in the order, and it may apply to the entire nation or just a specific region.
 
• It should be presented for approval to each House of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Article 366:**
 
 
• It states that an **Anglo-Indian** is someone whose father or any other male progenitors in the male line are or were of European descent, but who is or was domiciled in India and is or was born there of parents who are habitually resident there and are not established there for temporary purposes only.
 
 
 
• **Article 358:**
 
 
• Article 358 of the Indian Constitution addresses the issue of suspending citizens' **fundamental rights**. 
 
• Citizens of India are granted a number of fundamental rights as outlined in Article 19 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• But in certain unique emergency situations, these fundamental rights may be curtailed.
